sentences.text: 4. It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners that petitioners are quite innocent and have committed no offence.
They have been falsely implicated in this case.

Petitioners were in the business of iron and steel in the name of Awadhesh Mahesh Iron Merchant situated at Raje Sultanpur, U.P. and being the supplier, they supplied goods to the complainant worth Rs.2.5 Lakhs,
for which the alleged payment was made by the complainant.
The receipt of the goods supplied is enclosed at Annexure-P/II series.
It is further submitted that this is a civil/money dispute between the parties.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the matter relates to the year 2003, the complaint case was filed in the year 2014 but the petitioners moved for anticipatory bail in 2024,
due to lack of knowledge regarding this case filed by the complainant.
Petitioners have no criminal antecedent.

5. Learned APP for the State as well as learned counsel for the O.P. No.2 opposed the prayer for bail by submitting that the receipts enclosed by the petitioners are forged and fabricated, there is no sign of the complainant over the receipts indicating therein that the said articles have been purchased by the complainant.

6. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.1550 of 2024(3) dt.16-04-2024 it appears that it is a civil/money dispute between the parties, as such, let the above named petitioners, be released on bail, in the event of their arrest or surrender before the learned Court below within a period of six weeks from today, on furnishing bail bond of Rs.
25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned court below where the case is pending/Successor Court in connection with Complaint Case No.26632 of 2014, subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2)
of the Cr.P.C.
(Anjani Kumar Sharan, J) pallavi/-
